payload.title: How to Get Married in Brazil as a Foreigner
payload.excerpt: Getting married in Brazil legally means the civil process at a Cartório de Registro Civil, the civil registry office. You apply to be cleared to marry, a step called the habilitação, then marry on a day, at a time and in a place the registrar sets with you.
key_takeaways: Brazilian law ties the marriage application, the habilitação, to the civil registry of the district where one of you resides, so your first question for the cartório, before flights or a venue, is whether and how a couple living abroad can apply.
Foreign documents generally need an apostille at home and then a sworn Portuguese translation that can only be done in Brazil, so build time in Brazil for it.
A religious ceremony can carry civil effect when the couple are cleared first and the marriage is registered within 30 days of the ceremony.

For Australians, a Certificate of No Impediment comes from DFAT or the Australian Embassy in Brasília, and an overseas marriage is in most cases recognised at home if it was valid where it took place.

faq.q: Can foreigners get married in Brazil?
faq.a: The legal route is the civil process at a Cartório de Registro Civil. You apply for the habilitação with the documents the civil law requires, at the civil registry of the district where one of you resides. If neither of you lives in Brazil, the first question for the cartório is whether and how you can apply, then how long to allow in Brazil.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get married in Brazil?
faq.a: It depends on your venue, guest numbers and dates. A fee applies for an Australian CNI and for the Embassy's notarial services, and the official pages linked in the cost section show the current amounts. Ask the cartório and the sworn translator for their charges in writing.

faq.q: Do we need a Certificate of No Impediment to marry in Brazil?
faq.a: For Australians: ask the cartório. DFAT advises confirming with the local authority whether a CNI is needed, whether a state or territory single status certificate will do instead, and whether it must be issued in Brazil or apostilled. The Australian Embassy in Brasília and the Consulate-General in São Paulo issue CNIs by appointment.

faq.q: Is a religious wedding in Brazil legally binding?
faq.a: It can be. You obtain the certificate of habilitação first, and the religious marriage is registered within 30 days of the ceremony at the registry office that issued it. Registration takes legal effect from the date of the ceremony.

faq.q: How many witnesses do we need?
faq.a: At least two, unless the law provides otherwise. Ask the cartório what it requires of them.

faq.q: Can we get married on a beach in Brazil?
faq.a: The civil marriage is held on the day, at the time and in the place you request and the registrar sets. Ask the cartório whether the presiding officer will come to the beach, and ask your venue who gives permission to use it.
